focus: Explain Bayes' rule for a binary diagnostic test. Control prevalence, sensitivity, and false-positive rate; show the numerator, evidence denominator, and posterior; explore rare conditions and improved specificity.
excerpt: Bayes' rule gives P(D|+) = P(+|D)P(D) / P(+). For a binary condition, P(+) = P(+|D)P(D) + P(+|not D)P(not D). The posterior therefore depends on both test characteristics and the prior prevalence.
